record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Quantum Information Theory
record.context_brief: Boundary of the quantum correlation body
record.original_question: In the (N, M, K) multipartite correlation setting with no-signalling polytope P, quantum correlation body Q, and classical local polytope C, consider the portion of the boundary of Q that is not already contained in the boundary of P. Can every point on that part of the quantum boundary be reached using K-dimensional local Hilbert spaces and complete von Neumann measurements with K orthogonal projectors on pure states of minimal dimension?

evidence.quote: Only obeying no-signalling and positivity constraints, we get the no-signalling polytope P. Contained in it is the convex body Q of correlations obtainable from a multipartite quantum state with quantum mechanical POVM measurements, and inside Q the polytope C of correlations realizable by a classical realistic theory

Problem 26.A:
Consider the part of the boundary of Q, which is not already contained in the boundary of P. Can one reach all these points by choosing each one of the local Hilbert spaces to be K-dimensional, and each measurement as a complete von Neumann measurement (with K orthogonal projectors) on pure states with minimal dimension?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix integers N, M, K ≥ 2. Consider an N-partite Bell-type scenario in which each party can choose one of M measurement settings, each with K possible outcomes. A correlation is the collection of joint outcome probabilities P(a_1,...,a_N | x_1,...,x_N), where x_i ∈ {1,...,M} is the setting and a_i ∈ {1,...,K} is the outcome of party i.

Define:
- P, the no-signalling polytope: the set of correlations that are non-negative, normalized, and satisfy the no-signalling conditions (the marginal distribution of any subset of parties is independent of the other parties' setting choices).
- Q ⊆ P, the quantum correlation body: the set of correlations of the form P(a_1,...,a_N | x_1,...,x_N) = Tr(ρ · E^{(1)}_{a_1|x_1} ⊗ ··· ⊗ E^{(N)}_{a_N|x_N}), where ρ is a density operator on a tensor product H_1 ⊗ ··· ⊗ H_N of (arbitrary finite-dimensional) Hilbert spaces and {E^{(i)}_{a|x}}_a is a POVM on H_i for each setting x.
- C ⊆ Q, the classical local polytope: correlations admitting a local hidden variable model.

Let ∂Q denote the boundary of Q and ∂P that of P, and consider the relative boundary ∂Q \ ∂P, i.e. quantum-boundary points not lying on the no-signalling boundary.

Question: Is it true that every point of ∂Q \ ∂P can be realized by a quantum model in which each local Hilbert space H_i has dimension exactly K and each local measurement is a complete von Neumann measurement consisting of K rank-one orthogonal projectors onto pure states?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem has been solved negatively. Vértesi and Pál (2008) exhibited Bell inequalities whose maximal quantum violation cannot be attained with two-qubit systems and rank-one projective measurements, showing that K-dimensional local Hilbert spaces with complete von Neumann measurements do not suffice to reach all points of the relevant part of ∂Q. This resolution is recorded on the IQOQI "Open Quantum Problems" page for Problem 26.A.

status_evidence.title: Bell inequalities holding for all quantum states – Open Quantum Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Problem 26.A was solved in [3]. ... the maximum value of the two-outcome Bell inequality cannot be reproduced by two-qubit systems.
status_evidence.claim: Problem 26.A is solved negatively: higher local Hilbert space dimensions (or non-projective measurements) are needed.

status_evidence.title: Quantum Correlations in the Minimal Scenario
status_evidence.snippet: Detailed analysis of the boundary of the quantum correlation body in the minimal Bell scenario, including non-exposed extreme points.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work characterizes the boundary structure of Q in agreement with the negative resolution.
